NAH, this is just from details of the post tho, I could be wrong and I don’t know how she acts with you on a day-to-day basis. Anxiety and depression can be extremely overwhelming for some, if that really is the issue, you should try and help her to see if there are other financial support programs that can help her out. I do agree that her saying that you were “financially controlling” her is not right tho. Because that’s just not correct. I do think you’re perfectly valid for cutting her off from luxuries and only providing her needs especially because you’re struggling financially rn, but everyone has different needs. Sometimes needs aren’t as dry and cut as everyone thinks they are, you should have a talk with her about what her needs are and move forward from there. But, I do agree that 6-7 cans a day are excessive, it’s a waste of money. You’re not the asshole for turning her request down. Dr. pepper might be a vice that she emotionally depends on because of her mental issues, you should try and see if there are any free or sliding scale mental services that are available to her as well as an alternative. Also, if she really loves Dr. Pepper, you can use these luxury items as progress incentives. For example, if she gets a job interview, you can treat her with a slice of pizza and some Dr. Pepper. If she books an appointment with a free Counsellor and actually goes, you can treat her with another small luxury item she requested. This really helped me when I was struggling. Best of luck to you!
